patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` is unrelated SHA-512 assembly churn and failed to apply to `/src/boringssl`, so it is not evidence for this SRTP path. The authoritative fixed `n132/arvo:42534993-fix` image is still a genuine witness for the frozen root obligation: on the saved original case it reaches both `srtp_profiles_handoff` and `srtp_strchr_sink` with `profile_cstring_initialized_prefix_bytes == profile_cstring_read_bytes == 24`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-code read on the vulnerable path. `GetString` consumes the next byte from the remaining `CBS` as an 8-bit length and aliases that many attacker-controlled bytes as `str`, creating the exact field that later becomes the SRTP profile string.

This call discards the explicit `CBS_len(&str)` bound and hands the operand to a parser that only understands NUL-terminated, colon-delimited C strings. On the witnessed path the payload is 23 spaces with no colon, so the downstream parser can terminate only when it reaches the string's trailing sentinel byte.

MSAN sink. `ssl_ctx_make_profiles` treats the caller-supplied buffer as a C string and asks `strchr` to scan from `ptr` until `:` or `\0`. For the witnessed 23-space payload there is no colon, so `strchr` reaches the trailing byte at offset 23, which MSAN reports as uninitialized.

edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records identical pointer values at `srtp_profiles_handoff.profile_cstr_ptr` and `srtp_strchr_sink.parser_input_ptr`.
